title: Your own voice
job: An eight-sentence piece that changes register midway
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: EACH ITEM IS AN EIGHT-SENTENCE PIECE WITH ONE TURN INSIDE IT, and the word bound applies to each sentence inside the piece and not to the piece. The turn is a REGISTER change and not a plot twist — L4-M10 owns the twist and this module must not repeat it. Four sentences in the course's own voice, one pivot, three in the formal register, and each half keeps its own rules on its own side of the switch.

THE BEST PIECES HAVE A PIVOT SENTENCE THAT BELONGS TO BOTH HALVES. ataḥ adhunā mayā ekam kāryam kartavyam is still about the speaker, so the neutral half has not ended, and it is already built on L4-M1's gerundive with its instrumental agent, so the formal half has already begun. A piece that changes register between two paragraphs is two pieces.

THE REGISTER CHIP ON A PIECE NAMES THE HIGHEST REGISTER IT REACHES. There is one chip per item and the register changes inside it, so the chip cannot follow the turn. It is set to formal on every piece here, because a piece carrying ucyate, kriyate and a gerundive is not a neutral piece — the chip warns the learner what is inside, and the notes say where the turn is.

WHAT THE FORMAL HALF IS MADE OF, all of it paid for already: L4-M7's agentless passive (kriyate, dīyate, ucyate), L4-M1's gerundive with mayā or bhavatā beside it, the long compound kāryālayasamayaḥ, the posted sūcanā and the niyamaḥ it states. Not one word in this module is new. That is the point of putting it last.

WHICH TWO REGISTERS, DECIDED RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN: NEUTRAL TO FORMAL, UPWARD. THE DOWNWARD SWITCH — NEUTRAL TO INTIMATE — IS REFUSED. The intimate register on this course is exactly one line, L2-M1's, and it is tvam plus a bare-stem imperative. Four intimate sentences would need the -si present, tava, tubhyam, tvām, te and the vocative: six things bought in the last rung of the last level with nothing after it to practise them on.

tvam STAYS AT EXACTLY ONE DISPLAY IN THE WHOLE COURSE, AND THE REASON IS SMALLER THAN THE BUDGET. L2-M1 paired it with āgaccha because tvam beside a THIRD-person verb teaches a false agreement — and every bare-stem imperative but āgaccha is written nowhere. So a second tvam line would have to buy a verb cell before it could be grammatical at all, and the cell it would buy is the first brick of the paradigm this course has refused fifty times.

English changes register mostly by swapping words — 'get' for 'obtain', 'so' for 'accordingly'. Here the words largely stay and the SYNTAX changes: the agent leaves the sentence, the passive arrives, the obligation is stated impersonally. A piece that only swaps nouns has not changed register, and that is this module's commonest failure.

English can drift up and down inside one paragraph without anybody noticing. Here the turn is audible, so it must be deliberate and it must happen once. Turning twice in eight sentences does not read as range; it reads as somebody who cannot hear which register they are in.

THE EXIT DISCIPLINE, TRUE ONLY HERE. There is no rung after this one, so a word this module leaves unpaid is unpaid forever. The cap is the level's 25, as it is everywhere, but the target here is ZERO: if a piece needs a word the ladder has not bought, the PIECE is rewritten. This module opens no new word at all.

STAYS OUT, named here because there is nowhere left to name it: tvam beyond L2-M1's one line; every -si present; tava, tubhyam, tvām, te; mā; the vocative; every imperfect but āsīt; agamiṣyat; the productive bare -ta participle; the plural participial past; svasā; mahat; asmi; -anīya; every bare-stem imperative but āgaccha; every optative cell beyond the seven L3-M4 and L4-M3 opened and L5-M6's vadet; and any new proper noun.

sentences.cue: First I went to the office in the morning. My friend was there. Then I did my work. Now it is evening. So there is one thing I must do now. Work is not done at the office in the evening. There is a notice saying entry is forbidden. So it is said that one must go home.
sentences.literal: first I in-the-morning office went. there my friend was. then I work did. now evening happened. so now by-me one work must-be-done. at-office in-the-evening work not is-done. entry forbidden quote notice is. so home must-be-gone-to quote is-said

words.note: L2-M10's first sequencer. It sits between sentences and never inside one, and it opens the neutral half of the piece.
L2-M6's 'by me', the agent L4-M1's gerundive takes. It is the first word of the pivot and the first word of the formal half.
L4-M1's gerundive of karoti, fixed neuter -am. It never agrees with mayā or with anything else, which is what makes it sound written.
L4-M7's passive of karoti. Nobody is named as doing it, and the agent that was in the sentence before has now left it.
L4-M7's 'forbidden', agreeing with praveśaḥ. It is one of only two bare -ta participles this course writes, and it is learned whole.
L4-M7's passive of saying. It closes the formal half by putting the obligation in nobody's mouth at all.

sentences.trap: The turn is at the fifth sentence and not at the sixth. mayā … kartavyam is still about the speaker's own evening, so the neutral half has not stopped; but the agent is already in the instrumental and the verb is already a gerundive, so the formal half has started. That overlap is what makes it one piece.

mistake.display: ataḥ adhunā aham ekam kāryam kartavyam.
mistake.why: A gerundive never takes a nominative agent. The moment kartavyam replaces karomi the person has to move to mayā, and that case change is half of what makes the register turn audible.

words.note: L1-M6's library as the place gone TO. The -am is the whole of 'to', and no word for it is written.
L4-M1's gerundive of paṭhati, keeping the i as paṭhitum and paṭhitvā do. Fixed neuter, agreeing with nobody.
L5-M3's conversation. In the formal half it is the subject of a passive verb, which is where an abstract noun does its heaviest work.
L4-M7's rule, masculine. It is what a notice is an instance of, and it sits in L1-M3's plain asti frame.
L5-M1's emphasiser, standing after the word it lifts. At the end of an obligation it is 'and nothing else'.

sentences.trap: The pivot here is a fact about the speaker's own habit and an obligation at the same time. Read it as the last neutral sentence and the piece works; read it as the first formal one and it works too — that is not an ambiguity, it is the join.

sentences.cue: This evening my friend came to the house and ate. I ate too. Then my friend told a story. Now it is late. So my friend must go home now. It is said that late in the evening the road is far. So one must go by vehicle. The rule is that this must certainly be done.

I also meal did. then friend story said. now evening happened. so now by-friend home must-be-gone-to. evening at-the-end road far is quote is-said. so by-vehicle indeed must-be-gone-to. this certainly must-be-done quote rule

words.note: L3-M1's absolutive of āgacchatu. A prefixed root takes -ya and never -tvā, which is the only reason its ending differs from gatvā's.
L2-M6's 'by a friend · with a friend'. Here it is the agent the gerundive takes, which is the same shape and a different job.
L4-M1's gerundive of gacchati. Fixed neuter -am: it never agrees with mitreṇa, with gṛham, or with anything else in the line.
L2-M4's vehicle in the 'by' shape. It answers katham — the question about means — and it needs no preposition in front of it.
L4-M4's 'certainly'. In an argument it concedes; in a rule it insists, and the word itself does not change.

sentences.trap: The pivot moves the agent off the speaker and onto the guest, and that is where the register turns. Everything before it is a host's account of an evening; everything after it is the reason the evening has to end.
sentences.sound: AD-ya SAA-yam MA-ma MIT-ram GRI-ham AA-ga-tya bho-JA-nam KRI-ta-vaan. The neutral half is said quickly and runs on; from mitreṇa onward the sentences shorten and the pauses at the full stops lengthen, and that is audible before any word is recognised.

words.note: L2-M2's sister, feminine, and the actor of the neutral half. Every participle about her ends -tavatī and none of them is a choice.
L1-M1's female teacher as the one asked. The -ām is what marks her as the object of the asking and nothing else does.
L5-M6's answer, neuter. It looks the same whether it is given or received, as every neuter noun on this course does.
L4-M1's 'by you' for a woman, and the agent of the gerundive here. The obligation is handed to the listener, which is where this piece turns.
L4-M7's passive of dadātu. The counter that issues the certificate goes unmentioned, and the thing issued becomes the subject.

sentences.trap: The pivot moves the obligation from the sister to the listener. It is the only piece in the module whose turn also changes who the piece is about, and it works because bhavatyā is both a polite address and a gerundive agent.

mistake.why: Every word is correct and the register never changes. vadanti names people doing the saying, so the last three sentences are still the speaker's own voice with different vocabulary — which is exactly the mistake this module exists to prevent. The passive is what takes the person out, and the person leaving IS the register change.

comprehensionPool.script: स्वस्ति भवते। अद्य भवतः विवाहः अस्ति। शुभम् अस्तु। मङ्गलम् अस्तु। अतः मया तत्र गन्तव्यम्। उत्सवे जनाः साधु साधु इति वदन्ति। मन्दिरे प्रवेशः प्रातः एव दीयते। अतः इदम् अवश्यम् कर्तव्यम्।

comprehensionPool.display: aham chātraḥ. aham saṃskṛtam śanaiḥ vadāmi. kṛpayā śanaiḥ vadatu. samasyā na asti. ataḥ mayā pratidinam paṭhitavyam. śāstre saṃskṛtam anyathā ucyate. sambhāṣaṇe evam na kriyate. ataḥ idam api paṭhitavyam.
comprehensionPool.cue: I am a student. I speak Sanskrit slowly. Please speak slowly. No problem. So I must study every day. Sanskrit is said differently in a treatise. That is not done in conversation. So this too must be studied.
comprehensionPool.script: अहम् छात्रः। अहम् संस्कृतम् शनैः वदामि। कृपया शनैः वदतु। समस्या न अस्ति। अतः मया प्रतिदिनम् पठितव्यम्। शास्त्रे संस्कृतम् अन्यथा उच्यते। सम्भाषणे एवम् न क्रियते। अतः इदम् अपि पठितव्यम्।
